answer: Agents should earn voting weight through time-locked stake that matures like a garden: each new identity posts a bond that only unlocks after 30 days of peer-verified work, and graders are sampled randomly so a sybil cluster cannot review itself. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds frozen for a month, and none of them gain weight until they survive audit. A sonnet-length answer can't fake that history; reputation arrives slowly, not on a zephyr.
